critic_summary: The single-candidate probe correctly fired FAIL on loop-3's tight-spread override but left the researcher with no escape valve when no alternative proposal was prepared — forcing a 'deliberate divergence' where the researcher ran the 12-date eval anyway, which is exactly the failure mode the gate was meant to prevent; compounding this, loop-3's hypothesis was a flag-inverted variation on loop-2's spread axis (loop-2 added skips at wide spread, loop-3 removed skips at tight spread), which the trace itself flagged as ambiguous. Both failures share one root cause: sequential single-proposal exploration with no breadth and no architectural diversity guard. The new method front-loads breadth: generate four candidates each on a different conditioning axis (with explicit ban on re-entering prior axes), rank by adversarial score (which counterargument is hardest to dismiss), probe the top two on the SAME single date for fair comparison, and use a tournament gate with an explicit escape valve — if both probes fail, proceed with the less-bad candidate to the 12-date eval rather than aborting, so the loop always produces gate-comparable metrics. If the new method works, the next reasoning trace should contain four distinct conditioning axes in NOTES.md, an adversarial ranking, six pre-committed numbers across the two probed candidates, and an explicit tournament-winner selection — not a single proposal extending the prior loop's axis.
